text:
The city at night is a canvas of light, each skyscraper a brushstroke of vibrant fluorescence against the deep indigo of the twilight sky, painting an urban masterpiece that wakes up as the rest of the world sleeps. Like a great, slumbering beast stirring in its den, the metropolis sheds its daytime skin of concrete and routine to reveal a luminous underbelly of neon and glass. The streets below are not merely roads but veins pulsing with the electric blood of commerce and desire, while the towering structures stand as silent sentinels, their windows blinking like the eyes of a thousand watchful giants. In this nocturnal theater, the darkness is not an absence but a velvet curtain, allowing the artificial stars of the skyline to perform their dazzling, unblinking ballet.

Regarding the priority question: The primary material of a candle is wax, which serves as the fuel source, typically combined with a wick made of braided cotton or other fibrous material that draws the melted wax upward to sustain the flame.
